title: KV slot drift scratchpad
body:
Purpose:
Quick personal log while chasing a recurring production-ish repro where long-context sessions (seqlen > 16k) show KV cache slot "drift" causing attention to point at stale keys. This is a scratchpad: commands, raw snippets, hypotheses, and minimal repro notes. Not polished.

High-level symptom:
- Customer session with streaming long prompt (~20k tokens) saw a sudden drop in model coherence after a clean prefix. Subsequent tokens reference earlier conversation fragments that should have been evicted or overwritten.
- Observed occasional error in logs on one node: "kv_slot_index overflow: index=65536 capacity=65536" then later an OOB read reported by ASAN on a debug build.

Quick reproduction attempts (local dev box):
1) baseline run (native runtime, quantized, 1xA100):
   - cmd: ./bin/infer --model=rw-7b --input=repro/prompt_long.txt --max-tokens=512 --seqlen=20480 --kernel-policy=auto --kv-cache=on
   - result: no crash, but qualitatively saw repeated tokens after ~14k tokens in prompt.

2) stress script (parallel sessions to provoke wrap behavior):
   - cmd: scripts/stress_kv.sh --sessions=8 --model=rw-7b --session-len=22000 --burst=50
   - result: after ~6 minutes one worker logged "kv-index-wrapped: session_id=... offset=4294967294" (unsigned wrap suspicion).

3) debug build with KV bounds checks enabled:
   - cmd: CGO_ENABLED=0 make debug && ./bin/infer_debug --model=... --seqlen=32000
   - observed ASAN trace: 
     "AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow on address 0x60200000efc8 at pc 0x7f8c...
      READ of size 8 at 0x60200000efc8 thread T0"
   - stack frames point to kv_index_read + 0x48 and attention_kernel_choose + 0xd4.

Raw log snippets (sanitized):
[2026-01-18 14:22:03.112] INFO session=jj-123 prompt_tokens=14752 kv_base=0 kv_top=14752
[2026-01-18 14:22:12.639] WARN session=jj-123 kv_slot_index overflow: index=14753 capacity=14752
[2026-01-18 14:22:12.640] ERROR session=jj-123 attention:kv-read OOB idx=14753 cap=14752 kernel=fused_attn_v2
[2026-01-18 14:22:12.642] DEBUG session=jj-123 kernel-choice: fallback->stable_lt32 (policy detected long seq)

Immediate observations:
- Index values near capacity look suspicious (off by one behavior).
- Kernel chooser flips to stable_lt32 after overflow event; could be reacting to an inconsistent seqlen/capacity read.
- One log shows an unsigned integer wrap (4294967294) which suggests a signed/unsigned mismatch in slot arithmetic when session offsets are converted.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Off-by-one in eviction pointer arithmetic when doing KV append for sequences that trigger chunked allocation (chunks of 16k). Edge at boundaries (exact multiples) cause write to next slot without expanding capacity.
2) Signed/unsigned mix in session->offset calculation yields huge numbers for negative delta, leading to wrap to large positive index.
3) Attention kernel selection path (auto) reads stale metadata (old capacity) because metadata update and kernel decision are not atomic. Kernel picks fused kernel expecting contiguous allocations but KV layout is partially reallocated.
4) Race between background compaction/eviction and real-time append when multiple threads push to the same session (e.g., multi-turn streaming with watermark checkpoints).
5) Corruption in the mapping table (kv_slot_map) due to linear probing failing after load factor passes threshold and rehash not properly synchronized.

Commands/patches tried so far:
- Added assert in kv_append: assert(offset <= capacity) and ran debug; reproduced assert in ~20% of stress runs.
- Force kernel-policy=stable_lt32 for all runs: reduced OOB but still saw strange attention jumps (coherence issues) without an explicit crash.
- Quick patch: change uint32_t -> int64_t on session offset arithmetic (local branch offset-int64-fix).
  - result: reduced unsigned wrap occurrences, but another run produced "kv_read stale metadata" (race-looking).
- Instrumented metadata updates with atomic_fence seq_cst (meta-fence branch). After this, stress runs didn't hit ASAN for ~50 runs but still occasionally see logical drift (no bounds violation).

Minimal repro notes (how to trigger locally):
1) Use model rw-7b quantized with chunked_kv=16k.
2) Run: scripts/repro_kv_wrap.py --seed=8243 --prompt-size=21000 --random-inserts --concurrent-writes=2
3) Look for logs: "kv_slot_index overflow" or attention referring to tokens from >8k earlier than expected.

Evidence for kernel selection issue:
- When kernel-choice prints fallback->stable_lt32 right after an overflow, the attention scores computed by fused_attn_v2 vs stable_lt32 differ in placement of softmax normalization and prefetch behavior. If policy flips mid-operation, cached prefetches could still reference previous layout.
- Dumped kernel metadata before/after overflow: kernel_meta.num_kv_blocks changed from 8 -> 7 while kv_base stayed the same in one trace. That mismatch is a red flag.

Short-term mitigations (customer-facing):
- Force per-session kernel policy override to stable_lt32 for sessions flagged as long-context until we ship fix.
- Increase KV capacity by 10% when seqlen > 16k as an emergency guard.

Next experimental steps (todo):
- [ ] Build a unit test that simulates chunk boundary appends with concurrent compaction; aim to reproduce in CI.
- [ ] Add CAS-based update for kernel metadata to avoid stale reads (meta-cas branch).
- [ ] Add verbose timeline logs: record (session_id, op_id, pre_meta, post_meta, thread_id) for every KV append/evict. Run stress and collect timeline traces.
- [ ] Run ASAN on higher parallelism (16 sessions) to see if race frequency increases.
- [ ] Schedule quick sync with Marisol (SRE) to correlate SLO drops with these events for affected customers (JIRA-RT-4521).

Notes for PR description if we land a fix:
- Explain the off-by-one root cause (if confirmed) and why chunked allocation boundary is special-case.
- Document atomicity requirements between kernel-choice and kv metadata updates.
- Add canary config to Redwood Console: auto-flag sessions using chunked_kv > 16k for aggressive telemetry.

Random observations/brain dump:
- Could the problem be exacerbated by client-side chunking that sends partial tokens causing multiple small appends rather than single large append? Need to audit streaming client logic.
- If eviction is cooperative (background compactor), there's a window where capacity is temporarily inconsistent; ensure kernel chooser checks current meta version and retries if mismatch.

Footer: incremental notes will go here as I re-run stress suite. If you touch kv_index math, ping me on Slack with test number.

End of scratchpad entry (Avery).
